title: Strings: Text That Owns Itself, and Views That Do Not

questions.question: What is the difference between std::string and std::string_view?
options: A string owns its characters, a view is a pointer and a length that owns nothing
A view is faster but holds fewer characters
A string is mutable, a view is a constant string
There is no difference in C++17
questions.explanation: It is exactly the span from lesson 01-04, specialised for text, and it carries the same warning: it keeps nothing alive.

questions.question: What does a failed find return, and why must it be checked?
options: npos, which is the largest possible size, so using it as a position reads far past the end
Zero, which would silently mean the first character
A negative number, which is safe to use
It throws an exception
questions.explanation: It is the same idea as nullptr and end(): a value that cannot be mistaken for a real answer, and that must never be used as one.

questions.question: Why does starts_with test the length before comparing?
options: A text shorter than the prefix would be compared past its own end
Because compare is slow
Because compare cannot handle empty strings
To make the function constant time
questions.explanation: The comparison is told how many characters to look at. If the text is shorter than that, the count runs off the end.

questions.question: Why does split produce an empty piece for two separators in a row?
options: A parser needs to see that a field was blank rather than have it disappear
Because the standard requires it
To keep the piece count even
It is a bug that nobody has fixed
questions.explanation: Silently dropping an empty field turns a malformed line into a plausible one, which is worse than reporting it.

questions.question: What is wrong with std::string_view view = std::string("temporary");
options: The string is destroyed at the end of the statement and the view points at released memory
A view cannot be created from a string
The string is copied unnecessarily
Nothing, this is the recommended form
questions.explanation: The temporary dies at the semicolon. It is the dangling span of lesson 01-04 in different clothing, and it is the one shape of this mistake that catches everybody.

questions.question: What is the rule these helpers all follow?
options: Take a view, return a string
Take a string, return a view
Take and return views everywhere for speed
Take and return strings everywhere for safety
questions.explanation: A view parameter copies nothing at the call site, and a string return leaves no question about who owns the result or how long it lives.
